BRN Threads

Usage: brn --data-dir ABSOLUTE_DIRECTORY COMMAND [--option VALUE]

Commands: init [--purpose test], records, notes, threads, needs-you, history, candidates, settings,
  projects [--trash yes]; project-create --title TITLE [--key KEY]
  project-chat --project ID --title TITLE; project-document --project ID --title TITLE --text MARKDOWN
  project-settings --project ID --base VERSION --title TITLE --instructions TEXT --knowledge yes|no
  chat-move --thread ID [--project ID|none]; project-link|project-unlink --project ID --note ID
  project-delete-preview --project ID (save JSON for review)
  project-delete --preview-file FILE --actions JSON [--key KEY]
  project-restore --project ID --base VERSION
  Project commands accept --key KEY for durable retry. Actions JSON maps each unfinished Action ID to Keep or Cancel.
  Search/connections accept --project ID; intake --intent project --project ID imports privately.
  intake --intent useful reuses the chat that already received the same source (in --project ID when given),
  unless work there is still running; then it starts a new chat (reused_chat false).
  note-create --title TITLE --text MARKDOWN
  thread-start --title TITLE
  read --id RECORD
  search --query TEXT [--limit 1..50] [--cursor NEXT] [--thread CHAT]
  connections --note ID [--hops 1|2] [--sources yes] [--thread CHAT]
  topics; topics-create; topics-choose --note ID
  knowledge-check [--seed-chat yes]
  model-install --destination ABSOLUTE_FRESH_FOLDER (native builds; downloads the pinned model)
  Semantic search uses the model folder named by BRN_EMBEDDING_MODEL_DIR.
  begin-edit --note ID --base VERSION [--token-out ABSOLUTE_NEW_FILE] (prints the session token once)
  update-buffer --session ID --generation N --text MARKDOWN --token-file ABSOLUTE_FILE|-
  save|discard --session ID --generation N --token-file ABSOLUTE_FILE|-; recovery
  reclaim-edit --session ID [--token-out ABSOLUTE_NEW_FILE] (test workspaces only)
  apply|dismiss --operation ID; undo --operation ID; archive|unarchive --thread ID
  queue --thread ID --text TEXT; keep-in-brn --note ID --base VERSION
  ask --thread ID --prompt TEXT [--budget 1..32] [--edit-note ID --base VERSION | --record-decision yes] [--trace summary|full]
  intake --source ABSOLUTE_FILE --intent useful|full|chat|project [--title TITLE] [--thread ID] [--project ID] [--trace summary|full]
  configure --provider Codex|Copilot --model ID --effort low|medium|high
    [--helper off | --helper-provider Codex|Copilot --helper-model ID --helper-effort low|medium|high
     [--helper-auth-file FILE|--helper-credentials-dir DIR]] (read-only research helper, off by default.
     Experimental: helper sub-agents are tested only with gpt-6-luna at high effort; other models may give unreliable results. Best for long-document digests; runs that delegate are slower)
  delegation --choice maintain|review-first
  pause; resume; export|backup --destination ABSOLUTE_FRESH_PATH
  restore --source ABSOLUTE_BACKUP
  upgrade --backup-directory ABSOLUTE_EXTERNAL_FOLDER

Choose delegation before resuming maintenance. Manual work remains available while pending.
Fresh explicit data only. Originals remain external; no external messages are sent.
Review apply and Undo are concrete owner actions. Continue uses ask on the same Thread.

Agents and scripts: brn --json --data-dir DIR COMMAND ... prints one JSON envelope on stdout.
  In --json mode: exit 0 ok, 1 internal, 2 usage, 3 stale, 4 deferred, 5 needs review, 6 rejected,
  7 failed (including busy and timeout), 130 interrupted (SIGINT), 143 terminated (SIGTERM).
  Without --json, failures exit 1 and outcomes such as Stale exit 0.
  --timeout SECONDS after --data-dir bounds the call; it never hides a commit (envelope stop).
  --actor NAME (or BRN_ACTOR) names the caller on the receipts this call commits; it is not identity.
  Every envelope reports authority {workspace_purpose, cli_authority, enforced: false, actor}.
  brn --json --help prints the machine contract (commands, options, outcomes, retry classes, error codes);
  brn [--json] COMMAND --help prints one command's help. --data-dir and --timeout may follow the command.
  Bounded inspection: history|candidates|records|notes|threads|needs-you|recovery --limit N [--cursor C],
  projects [--trash yes] --limit N, messages --thread ID, revisions --note ID,
  revision --note ID --version V, runs [--thread ID] [--state STATE], read --id ID --limit BYTES;
  pass result.cursor back as --cursor for the next page. operation --id OP | --key K --command NAME
  shows whether an operation (or a keyed command's key) applied, without using the key.
  Text options --title, --text, --prompt, --instructions, --actions also accept --NAME-file ABSOLUTE_FILE or --NAME-file - (stdin).
  --key KEY makes note-create, thread-start, undo, queue, archive|resolve, unarchive, keep-in-brn,
  intake --intent full|chat|project, topics-create, knowledge-check --seed-chat yes and project commands
  replay on retry. resolve is an alias of archive. A keyed full/chat/project intake replays when bytes,
  path, scope and title match a committed import, without converting or sending the document again;
  if that import found the bytes already imported, the retry converts again and records only an observation.
  Edit writes need the session token: begin-edit --token-out FILE, then --token-file FILE (never argv).
  Stale save (exit 3): keep result.session.markdown; discard your session (--token-file OLD); begin-edit --base
  <conflict[0].version> --token-out NEW; reapply; update-buffer --generation 1 --text-file merged.md --token-file NEW;
  save --generation 1 --token-file NEW.
  upgrade_required (exit 6): the workspace has an older schema and nothing changed; the CLI never upgrades
  implicitly. On the owner's instruction: brn --data-dir DIR upgrade --backup-directory ABSOLUTE_DIR (backs up first).
  intake --intent chat --thread <PROJECT_ID> attaches the document to that project: an owner decision.
  Commands marked owner_decision record an owner decision. Running the CLI does not make you the owner:
  run them only on the owner's explicit instruction for that exact operation.
